summary: Great Mills tower built 1933 as a 120-ft galvanized steel lookout; by 2006 the property went to St. Mary's County and the tower was reassembled at the MCPS Lathrop E. Smith center.

facts.design: Galvanized steel lookout tower, 120 ft high when built in 1933
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab no longer in place (Standing*)
facts.agency: Montgomery County Public Schools (owns and runs the Lathrop E. Smith center where the tower now stands)

access.note: School system outdoor education site; the sources read describe school programs, not public visits

events.note: Erected in summer 1933 as a 120-ft galvanized steel lookout (Midland Journal, Nov 10, 1933); Evening Star, Nov 18, 1933, reported it completed as the tallest fire tower west of Chesapeake Bay in Maryland
DNR had transferred ownership of the entire property to St. Mary's County by 2006
Structure removed and reassembled for new duties at the Lathrop E. Smith Environmental Education Center, Montgomery County; DNR gives no date

notes_for_editor: The DNR report is marked DRAFT and its Great Mills entry reads 'do date' (sic). The 'by 2006' phrase dates the property transfer, not the tower move; the report covers towers managed by DNR as of December 2006. Current height is not given in any source read, so height_m is left unset; the design line carries the 1933 height. Parent record data/towers/md/us-md-great-mills.json has height_m 36.6, which is the 1933 height. The DNR report says Rockville while MCPS gives a Meadowside Lane address; both are consistent with Montgomery County. The 1933 newspaper texts were read only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No staffing or fire records were found.
